video_title: Steph Curry wants NO DRAMA amid Warriors contract extension talks | NBA Today

quotes.speaker: Shams Charania
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen Curry's contract extension options with the Golden State Warriors
quotes.excerpt: This is in a completely different place than the Carl Anthony Towns of the Knicks situation is at.
quotes.quote: This is in a completely different place than the Carl Anthony Towns of the Knicks situation is at. The ball, according to one Warriors source to me this week, is totally in Stephen Curry's court. They have given him a slew of options to take. He has one-year deals, two-year deals, max deals. He has slightly under the max, where he would be giving the team a discount, some more flexibility. He has player option deals as well. So he has all the options, but another option that Stephen Curry has, not contractually right now, is potentially waiting into the season or waiting until next offseason when the Warriors, if Stephen Curry waits, would have about $100 million in cap space.

quotes.speaker: Malika Andrews
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen Curry's goals for the upcoming Warriors season
quotes.excerpt: He wants no drama, he wants some future flexibility, and he wants the best chance to win.

text_blocks.speaker: Malika Andrews
text_blocks.text: It seems like what Steph is saying is that he wants three things. He says he wants no drama, he wants some future flexibility, and he wants the best chance in absolute desperation to be able to win. That is a lot. How are the Warriors planning to achieve all of that?

text_blocks.speaker: Anthony Slater
text_blocks.text: Let's start with the no drama part. Go back to this time exactly last year, they were deep in a contract dispute with Jonathan Kuminga to the point that remember Al Horford and De'Anthony Melton couldn't go to Media Day, missed the first couple practices, or you go back to Klay Thompson's last couple years with the Warriors and the way that contract disputes with Klay Thompson really marred the end of Klay Thompson's time there. So to that point, Stephen Curry has seen the way contract drama can overtake a season, and this is him laying the edict before next week when we all ask him about it that, hey, there will be no drama.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst's advice on Stephen Curry's contract extension
quotes.excerpt: If Stephen Curry is willing to take less than the max contract, don't sign.
quotes.quote: If Stephen Curry is willing to take less than the max contract, don't sign. If he wants the max, which he has absolutely earned 100 times over, sign. That is it. So if he doesn't sign, actions over words. He doesn't even have to say. We know that he might be open to taking less than the max. This just happened with Draymond Green. Draymond opted out of his contract, it was a little bit of a trial run for the Warriors. They were trying to sign LeBron James or other players, they weren't able to do that, and they gave Draymond the exact same money back. This is Steph potentially doing the same thing. If you don't sign, it opens up a world of possibilities.

quotes.speaker: Anthony Slater
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen Curry's commitment to the Golden State Warriors
quotes.excerpt: The reason that Steph did the interview with Slater is to reiterate his career-long commitment to the Warriors.
quotes.quote: The reason that Steph did the interview with Slater is to reiterate his career-long commitment to the Warriors, to nip in the bud any discussion that leaving is even a consideration for him. And so, no worry about that. Waiting is actually good news for Golden State because that shows a willingness to be flexible, to work with the front office to try to rebuild that thing into a contender, which I think there's a very narrow path, frankly, for that to happen.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson on Stephen Curry's competitive mindset
quotes.excerpt: I expect Steph to do this. He's a winner. We saw and complimented Jalen Brunson for doing this.
quotes.quote: I expect Steph to do this. He's a winner. We saw and complimented Jalen Brunson for doing this. All the guys that do stuff like this take a little bit of a cut and make sure that they go out there and win. Always loved them. Steph, we've had our battles, but go get your money if you're going to get it. If not, hey man, I hope you go out winning and doing your thing in the playoffs and not having to be on a team that's just not competitive.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on Stephen Curry and Draymond Green's turnover focus
quotes.excerpt: It's frankly the Warriors aren't good enough to let Steph turn the ball over like crazy.
quotes.quote: Recently talked with Stephen Curry and he said, hey, for years, decades, I've been not getting on Draymond, you Draymond and Steph about turnovers. That's over. It's frankly the Warriors aren't good enough to let Steph turn the ball over like crazy. And he also said he wanted Draymond to shoot a bunch of threes, which Draymond said no one's ever told him before. So it looks like the Warriors are trying to figure out the, forget about the contract stuff. On the court, they're trying to figure out a pathway, how can we get ourselves to the play-in?

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson on the Warriors' turnover-prone style
quotes.excerpt: Part of playing against Steph and Draymond, you know that they're going to have three turnovers.
quotes.quote: Part of playing against Steph and Draymond, you know that they're going to have three turnovers, but it has no weight. They're going to have four turnovers, but it has no weight. If I come in the game or one of the other guys on our team at the time would have came in and they have three turnovers, it's different because we don't play like that. They played like that their whole careers. They play free flow, so it made them dangerous. To hear about an efficient Stephen Curry, an efficient Draymond Green, I don't even know what that looks like, but I know it takes the danger down.
